title: Match the promise at entry
trigger: A paid campaign promises one outcome but lands on a generic product introduction.
action: Give each approved campaign a landing variant that repeats its specific outcome, audience and eligibility in the first view. Carry any material offer condition into the page rather than making visitors rediscover it.
mechanism: Recognition may reduce the effort of confirming that the promised offer is here.
guardrail: Use only verified campaign claims; preserve a useful default for missing or invalid campaign parameters.
measure: Paid subscriptions per campaign entrant; misleading-offer complaints.

title: Route searchers by decision stage
trigger: Educational, comparison and purchase queries all lead to the same sales-heavy page.
action: Create distinct entry routes for learning the problem, comparing solutions and choosing an offer. Give each route the information needed for that stage and a clear bridge to the next, without forcing account creation.
mechanism: Matching readiness may reduce resistance from asking for commitment too early.
guardrail: Keep essential pricing accessible from every route; do not infer readiness from sensitive characteristics.
measure: Qualified progression and paid conversion by entry intent; early exits.

title: Deep-link to the promised capability
trigger: An integration or feature advertisement opens the homepage and makes visitors search again.
action: Send the verified feature-specific link to the relevant section or page, with the capability explanation visible on arrival. Retain product identity and a route to the full offer so the visitor can evaluate the larger product.
mechanism: Continuity may prevent the attention loss caused by repeating a search.
guardrail: Test the destination on direct load, mobile and back navigation; avoid anchors hidden under fixed headers.
measure: Paid conversion from feature entries; immediate return-to-source rate.

title: Build factual competitor evaluation pages
trigger: Qualified visitors search for a named competitor alternative but find only broad marketing claims.
action: Create a dated comparison using real buyer criteria, verified differences and the situations each product suits. Include migration prerequisites and links to the underlying facts, so the page answers an actual replacement decision.
mechanism: A relevant comparison can give buyers a usable reference for evaluating differentiation.
guardrail: Recheck competitor facts before publication; include meaningful weaknesses and avoid fabricated disadvantages or fake discounts.
measure: Qualified purchases from comparison traffic; mismatch refunds and corrections.

title: Bridge instructional content to product use
trigger: Tutorial readers receive useful advice but never see how the product performs that same task.
action: At the point where a tutorial's manual process becomes repetitive, show the equivalent supported product workflow and its input/output. Let readers continue the free instructions while offering a relevant route into the product.
mechanism: A contextual bridge may turn existing task motivation into product consideration.
guardrail: Keep the tutorial useful on its own; do not introduce an unrelated lead magnet or exaggerate manual difficulty.
measure: Activated paid accounts from tutorial readers; content task completion.

title: Target a genuine buying event
trigger: The page addresses an abstract audience rather than the event that makes them seek software now.
action: Build an entry page around a documented trigger such as a first client handoff, a growing approval queue or an upcoming reporting cycle. Explain what changes during that event and how the current product helps.
mechanism: Situation relevance may make the benefit feel immediate without manufactured urgency.
guardrail: Use real recurring buyer situations; do not invent a personal deadline or imply knowledge of an individual's circumstances.
measure: Qualified paid conversion from trigger pages; expectation mismatch.

title: Give integration visitors a direct route
trigger: People arriving from an integration listing must navigate several pages to confirm whether their connection is supported.
action: Create an integration-specific entry that names the supported account type, data direction, setup requirements and a real example. Link directly to the appropriate evaluation path while retaining the complete product and pricing context.
mechanism: Reduced compatibility uncertainty may help visitors who already know their required ecosystem.
guardrail: Verify current integration scope and plan restrictions; distinguish native integration, export and third-party automation.
measure: Integration-entry paid conversion; setup failures and support burden.

title: Preserve a deliberate comparison context
trigger: A buyer selects comparison criteria or a use case, then loses that context when opening detail pages.
action: Carry the visitor's explicit evaluation context in a shareable route or non-sensitive state. Returning to the comparison should restore the chosen criteria and location, making it easy to continue evaluating rather than rebuild the view.
mechanism: Reduced memory work may support considered purchases across multiple page visits.
guardrail: Do not silently select a paid plan or store sensitive evaluation inputs; provide a way to reset the view.
measure: Return-visit purchase completion; unintended-selection reports.

title: Explain the referring relationship immediately
trigger: A partner, affiliate or invited visitor lands without understanding why the product is relevant to the referring service.
action: Use an approved referral entry to explain the specific relationship and connected workflow, then present the ordinary product terms. Make any referral incentive and eligibility explicit where it affects the visitor's offer.
mechanism: A coherent handoff may transfer relevant context while reducing uncertainty about the destination.
guardrail: Verify the relationship and permissions; do not imply endorsement beyond the actual agreement.
measure: Referral-entry paid conversion; incentive confusion and refunds.

title: Keep marketplace and site promises aligned
trigger: Marketplace descriptions, screenshots and feature availability disagree with the website after product changes.
action: Audit the approved marketplace listing against the current offer and update outdated capabilities, prices or setup requirements through the authorized publishing workflow. Make the landing page continue the same workflow demonstrated in the listing.
mechanism: Consistent expectations may reduce abandonment caused by discovering a different offer.
guardrail: Confirm the listing's publication scope and review process; do not claim that an unapproved update is live.
measure: Marketplace-referred paid activation; discrepancy complaints.

title: Make regional eligibility clear at entry
trigger: Visitors from unsupported regions spend time evaluating before learning that purchase or service is unavailable.
action: Show supported regions, languages and relevant availability conditions near the entry information, using an editable region selector when useful. Give unsupported visitors an accurate alternative or notification option rather than a purchase path that fails later.
mechanism: Early fit information may preserve trust and concentrate effort on viable buyers.
guardrail: Do not infer citizenship or use sensitive traits; verify actual availability and obtain authorization before collecting notification details.
measure: Eligible paid conversion; late availability failures.

title: Continue the webinar's demonstrated workflow
trigger: People leaving an educational webinar arrive on a page unrelated to the workflow they just watched.
action: Prepare a dated companion page containing the demonstrated workflow, current product example and relevant plan information. Preserve the promised learning material, and make the transition from example to real use explicit.
mechanism: Familiarity and task continuity may help existing interest become a purchase decision.
guardrail: Use only licensed material and actual webinar claims; do not invent attendee proof or send follow-ups without authorization.
measure: Webinar-entry activation and paid conversion; promise-related support.

title: Recover expired campaign destinations honestly
trigger: Old campaign links lead to an expired offer, an error or a misleading still-active promotion.
action: Keep the destination useful by stating that the dated offer ended and presenting the current verified offer. Preserve the original topic and explain material differences so an interested visitor can still make a decision.
mechanism: A clear recovery path may salvage qualified demand without bait-and-switch confusion.
guardrail: Do not silently retain an expired discount or restart its timer; check all linked terms and checkout identifiers.
measure: Paid purchases from expired links; promotion disputes.

title: Carry desktop evaluation across devices
trigger: A desktop-only product receives mobile visitors who cannot install or use it immediately.
action: Offer a user-controlled way to continue on a suitable device, such as copying a stable setup link or displaying a QR code where appropriate. Preserve the chosen workflow without implying that the mobile device can run the product.
mechanism: Reducing the cost of postponement may keep genuine intent from disappearing between devices.
guardrail: Do not auto-email or create accounts; exclude private data and unsupported device claims from shared links.
measure: Cross-device activated purchases; broken handoffs.

title: Qualify the input the product needs
trigger: Entry traffic includes people who lack an essential data source, permission or supported file type.
action: State the required input beside the use case before the purchase path, with one recognizable example. Provide a preparation route when the missing prerequisite can be obtained, and a clear limitation when it cannot.
mechanism: Early qualification may reduce wasted evaluation and subsequent purchase regret.
guardrail: Verify that the prerequisite is truly required now; avoid making optional setup sound mandatory.
measure: Qualified paid activation; prerequisite-related refunds.

title: Keep shared links understandable without history
trigger: A prospect opens a colleague's product link but sees a page that assumes prior navigation or private context.
action: Make shared evaluation URLs open a self-contained view with product identity, the referenced example and its assumptions. Include enough context to understand the comparison without exposing the original visitor's private inputs or account state.
mechanism: Independent comprehension may help interest spread across a buying group.
guardrail: Validate public permissions and URL contents; require authentication for genuinely private artifacts.
measure: Shared-link qualified purchases; accidental exposure or confusion.

title: Explain legitimate product renames at entry
trigger: Qualified visitors arrive through an older product name and cannot tell whether the unfamiliar destination is still the service they intended.
action: Maintain an accurate old-name entry explanation and route legacy links to the matching current product or capability. State the rename or ownership change plainly, preserving useful evaluation context instead of sending every old link to an unexplained homepage.
mechanism: Continuity of identity may reduce uncertainty and distrust during an otherwise legitimate buying journey.
guardrail: Verify the actual relationship and current availability; do not imply unchanged ownership, contracts or features when those also changed.
measure: Paid conversion from legacy-name entries; identity and destination confusion.

title: Present a useful destination after public sharing
trigger: Public reports, templates or exported artifacts attract viewers, but their product link lands on an unexplained signup screen.
action: Create a viewer landing that explains how the shared artifact was made and offers a matching sample workflow. Let visitors inspect the original public artifact before deciding whether to create their own.
mechanism: Seeing a relevant outcome may make the product's value concrete for new entrants.
guardrail: Respect the creator's sharing permissions and branding settings; never expose private content as acquisition material.
measure: Viewer-to-paid activation; sharing-related privacy complaints.

title: Respect an explicit language selection
trigger: Visitors choose a language but campaign redirects or page navigation revert them to an unfamiliar version.
action: Preserve the declared language across marketing, pricing and entry routes, with a visible way to change it. Where the product itself has narrower language support, state that boundary before purchase rather than implying complete localization.
mechanism: Reduced comprehension effort may help visitors finish a considered evaluation.
guardrail: Verify translated prices and terms against the source; do not imply unsupported product languages or use unreliable auto-translation for commitments.
measure: Paid conversion by supported language; translation-related support.

title: Match specialist traffic to specialist evidence
trigger: A technical article attracts practitioners, but its destination removes the API, architecture or workflow details they came to evaluate.
action: Provide a specialist entry with the relevant working example, current documentation and deployment prerequisites, alongside a short explanation for nontechnical collaborators. Retain the normal offer path without requiring a sales conversation to inspect basic fit.
mechanism: Depth appropriate to intent may turn technical credibility into qualified buying interest.
guardrail: Keep examples compatible with the actual product version; avoid exposing secrets or implying production readiness from a toy example.
measure: Technically qualified paid activation; integration abandonment.
